Join me in just 30 minutes (!!) at 5:30 PM Eastern TODAY for this public virtual talk about immigration data with Mercy University. The link is available at the event announcement below, registration is NOT required - so just show up!  

austinkocher.substack.com/p/…
Read more on my Substack: austinkocher.substack.com

What the data doesn't yet tell us: how many arrested immigrants had any prior criminal contact, how many were removed without full adjudication, and how much fear is producing unmeasured effects thinning congregations, closed stalls, kids kept home.

The arrests concentrated geographically. More immigration arrests happened in and around Parkway Village than anywhere else in Memphis a majority-Black neighborhood that is also one of the city's fastest-growing Hispanic communities.

Per MPD's own data, Memphis crime had already fallen steadily since 2023, hitting a 25-year low before the task force began last fall. This matters for the causal story. Any claim the task force is "driving down crime" has to contend with the trend that preceded it.

About 4 in 5 of the immigration arrests followed traffic stops usually Tennessee Highway Patrol stops for minor violations like a broken taillight or tinted windows.
Federal agents often rode with or followed troopers, interrogating drivers and passengers afterward.

The broader picture: just over a quarter of the task force's 5,200 total arrests were for violent crimes, and most of those stemmed from outstanding warrants not new incidents. The operation is doing something just not mostly what it was announced to do.

800+ immigrants arrested. 17 (2%) charged with a violent crime. That's the Memphis Safe Task Force's first 4 months.
Source: propublica.org/article/memph…

You're invited on Thursday, April 23 at 12:30 PM, to hear from California Congressman Mike Levin about what he saw inside Otay Mesa Detention Center and why Americans should be paying attention.

What the data doesn't yet tell us: how often 287(g) officers operate outside authorized jurisdiction, and how ambient behavior reshapes school attendance, clinic visits, and public life in counties with no formal agreement. This is a measurement gap worth closing.
The ACLU estimates 77 million people (32% of the U.S.) now live in a county with at least one 287(g) agency. But the Gratis case is a reminder: the reach of the program isn't bounded by its MOAs.

For scale: as of April 17, 2026, ICE has signed 1,697 287(g) agreements across 39 states, up from 135 before January 2025. 1,028 are Task Force Model agreements, the aggressive form that deputizes officers during routine policing. Gratis PD signed one in Nov. 2025.

ICE told reporters this wasn't an enforcement action, citing its Nov. 2025 UAC Safety Verification Initiative, which lets 287(g) partners check on unaccompanied minors placed with sponsors. Even so: Gratis PD's jurisdiction doesn't include Hamilton County.

Chief Tonina Lamanna and Officer Jeffrey Baylor visited Western Hills UHS, Rees E. Price, and Roberts Academy on April 15, claiming to be with ICE. CPS staff asked them to leave. Cincinnati PD wasn't notified. Both are now on administrative leave.

A Gratis, Ohio police chief drove an hour to Cincinnati last week, visited 3 public schools, and claimed ICE authority to do "wellness checks." Gratis has a 287(g) agreement. Hamilton County does not. This is what 287(g) drift looks like.

You're invited on Thursday, April 23 at 12:30 PM, to hear from California Congressman Mike Levin about what he saw inside Otay Mesa Detention Center and why Americans should be paying attention.

A fed judge already blocked construction at the Hagerstown site in March 2026 on environmental grounds DHS had not conducted a National Environmental Policy Act review before beginning work on a $102 million warehouse purchase. 
austinkocher.substack.com/p/a-federal-...

There's also a revolving door worth flagging. David Venturella, who recently joined ICE after leaving GEO Group, is now leading the division that oversees detention contracts while GEO bids on warehouse work. Attorney General Pam Bondi is a former GEO lobbyist.

The timeline is aggressive. DHS wants the first warehouse facility accepting detainees this month. Some planned buildings will hold 7,000–10,000 people, rivaling the capacity of Las Vegas resorts and far exceeding the typical 1,800-person existing facility.
